crisis.label: High
crisis.detail: Sep 4: VP Vance told reporters Sep 3 that Iran's control of the Strait of Hormuz is 'effectively gone,' a 'diminishing asset,' and ruled out talks with Tehran unless it halts attacks on commercial shipping (Time, Washington Times). Kpler data reported by Business Recorder undercut the claim: only ~5 vessels transited Hormuz on Sep 1, versus a 10-day average of ~14, with no liquid tankers among them. Vance also voiced 'extreme skepticism' of Iran's account that a Sep 1 US strike killed 4-5 people at a Kuhestak (Sirik) wedding; Hormozgan officials named four victims, including a 4-year-old, with 60+ wounded (Al Jazeera). No new attacks are reported since Sep 2. Brent held at $95.81 (-0.12%) and WTI at $91.82 (+0.32%) on Sep 3 (Trading Economics); JKM CFD rose to $24.09 (+1.39%, Trading Economics); TTF eased to 71.15 EUR/MWh (-0.92%, Yahoo Finance). QatarEnergy force majeure remains extended into early November. Crisis level holds at 4 (High) given no new attack or Hormuz closure event; probabilities unchanged: base 5%, stress 50%, tail 45%.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: Iran and Oman advance a temporary corridor and mine-clearance framework; a signed, monitored reopening restores traffic and lowers Brent toward $75-85, while Qatar's force majeure keeps LNG availability constrained into early November.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: The corridor remains provisional and traffic stays selective under Iranian fees, sanctions pressure and residual mine and attack risk; Brent holds $85-105 and JKM stays elevated while Qatar's force majeure runs into early November.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: A widened multi-front exchange, a failed framework or renewed tanker attacks could close the southern lane again and spill into Bab el-Mandeb; Brent returns to $105-135+/bbl and JKM moves above $30/MMBtu.
